patients.summary: Unemployed former stock clerk with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes who joins in 2022 and is found to have syphilitic aortitis with aortic regurgitation, then ankylosing spondylitis. Repeated MSSA infections (foot ulcer bacteremia, mitral then aortic endocarditis) lead to heart failure and aortic root and valve replacement in late 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M transferring care. Wants a doctor who will actually pick up the phone.

CC: diabetes, and winded on stairs for the last few months.

HPI: Says the sugars have never been good. On metformin 1000 twice a day and glargine 30 units at night, takes both most days, misses the evening metformin when he skips supper. Doesn't check fingersticks much, meter is somewhere. No hypoglycemia that he knows of. Separately, since around the holidays he gets short of breath going up the two flights to his apartment and is more tired than he thinks he should be. No chest pain. Feels his heart thump sometimes. No leg swelling noticed.

PMH (per pt, old records requested): T2DM. Low back pain for years, worse mornings, uses naproxen when it flares. Eye inflammation (uveitis) several times in the past, treated with drops by an eye doctor, nothing in over a year. Mouth canker sores that come and go. Told he had syphilis around age 25 at a clinic; he never went back for the shots. Used IV drugs years ago, none in a long time, not interested in discussing further today but open about it.
PSH: tooth pulled at 20. Right thigh abscess drained at 40.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 30u qHS, lisinopril 10 daily, naproxen 250 BID prn.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father diabetic from age 50. Mother high blood pressure. Brother has ankylosing spondylitis. Father's father had an AAA.
SH: lives alone, apartment. Out of work, last job stocking shelves in a warehouse. Smokes about half a pack a day, has for ~15 yrs. Drinks once or twice a month. COVID shots x2 last spring.

ROS: + exertional dyspnea, fatigue, occasional pounding heartbeat. No fever, weight change, orthopnea, syncope. No vision changes or red eye now.

Exam: Thin-ish, comfortable at rest. BP 144/56, HR 104, rest of vitals in flowsheet. Bounding radial pulse. Heart: tachycardic, regular, soft blowing diastolic murmur along the left sternal border, no gallop. Lungs clear. No JVD. Abd benign. Ext: no edema, feet with intact skin, monofilament normal, pulses palpable. Spine: stiff with forward bending, nontender.

A/P:
1. Diastolic murmur with wide pulse pressure and exertional symptoms. Concerned about aortic regurgitation. Referring to cardiology for exam and echo, asked them to see him soon. Given the syphilis history, checking RPR with treponemal antibody today.
2. T2DM, poorly controlled by history. A1c, CMP, lipids, urine microalbumin today. Will adjust once I see numbers and his records.
3. Back pain: long-standing, continue naproxen as he uses it. Will revisit.
4. Tobacco: advised to quit, not ready. Will keep asking.
5. Screening: HIV, hep C, hep B serologies today. Colon screening and vaccines next visit.
Return 3 months, sooner after cardiology.

orders.reason: reactive RPR 1:8 and treponemal antibody, untreated syphilis, suspected aortic involvement

documents.title: Result note: new patient labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR reactive at 1:8 with reactive treponemal antibody, fits the untreated syphilis he described. Has never been treated, and with the murmur I want ID involved before anyone gives penicillin so they can decide on a spinal tap. Referral placed. A1c 9.4. HIV, hep C, hep B surface antigen all nonreactive; not immune to hep B, will vaccinate. Kidney function and blood count fine.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Christopher, your blood work is back. The syphilis test is positive, which matches what you told me. It has never been treated, so I am sending you to an infectious disease doctor who will treat it, likely with a short series of penicillin shots. Their office will call you. Your A1c (3 month sugar average) is 9.4, which is high; we will work on that together. Your kidneys and blood counts look good. You are not immune to hepatitis B, so I will offer that vaccine at your next visit. Call or text if you want to talk any of this over.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. i kind of figured. will that be why my heart is acting up

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It might be part of it. Untreated syphilis can affect the aorta and the valve next to it. The cardiologist and the echo will tell us. Keep that appointment.

reports.conclusion: Aortic root dilatation with aortic regurgitation. Mitral valve prolapse.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation (received 5/31/2022)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit date 05/09/2022.

Reason for consult: murmur and exertional symptoms, referred by primary care.

History: 45-year-old man who has had shortness of breath and fatigue with exertion for roughly half a year, plus intermittent palpitations; at night he notices his heart racing. Primary care checked syphilis serology, reactive. He reports an untreated syphilis diagnosis about two decades ago.

Medications at visit: metformin, insulin glargine, lisinopril, naproxen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: current smoker, half a pack daily; rare alcohol.
Family: paternal grandfather with AAA.

Exam: BP 145/55, pulse 110 and collapsing in quality. On auscultation there is a high-pitched blowing early diastolic murmur at the left sternal border, third interspace, loudest with him sitting up and leaning forward at end-expiration. Lungs clear. No edema.

Studies today: Chest radiograph with a dilated ascending aorta. Echocardiogram with aortic root dilatation and aortic regurgitation; incidental mitral valve prolapse.

Impression:
1. Syphilitic aortitis with aortic root dilatation.
2. Aortic regurgitation.
3. Mitral valve prolapse.

Plan: Start carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily and aspirin 81 mg daily. Agree with infectious disease evaluation and treatment of syphilis. Return in about a year or sooner with symptoms. Smoking cessation strongly advised.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Med reconciliation after cardiology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Cardiology letter came in today. Called pt to reconcile: he did start carvedilol 6.25 twice a day and aspirin 81 after that visit on 5/9, filled the same day. Some lightheadedness the first few days, now gone. Updated med list. He has ID appointment 6/6. Reminded about diabetes visit end of June.

documents.title: Infectious disease consultation (received 6/10/2022)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Seen 06/06/2022, with follow-up injections 06/13 and 06/20.

Question: reactive RPR 1:8 and treponemal antibody in a man with untreated syphilis remotely and newly found aortic root dilatation with aortic regurgitation.

Assessment: late (tertiary) syphilis with cardiovascular involvement. No headache, visual change, hearing loss, gait problem or memory complaint; neurologic examination normal. Given the cardiovascular disease, we performed a lumbar puncture today to exclude neurosyphilis: CSF white cell count and protein within normal limits, CSF VDRL nonreactive.

Plan: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly for three doses. First dose given today without reaction; he was observed afterward and counseled on possible fever and aches in the first day. Repeat RPR at 6, 12 and 24 months; we would expect at least a fourfold fall in titer. Can be drawn at his primary care lab with results to us.

Allergies: NKDA. HIV negative per PCP records.

Addendum 06/20/2022: third and final dose administered. Course complete.

- Vaccines: Heplisav #1 today, second in a month. PCV20 and Tdap also today.
- Colon screening: FIT kit given, he would rather that than a scope.
- Smoking: not ready.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back for the back pain we put off last time. Also new breathing complaint.

Back: lower back, years. Worst first thing in the morning and after sitting; loosens up when he walks around or does stretches, and lying in bed doesn't help at all. Naproxen takes the edge off. Also sore at the back of both heels. Brother has ankylosing spondylitis.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Lumbar spine: forward flexion and side bending clearly limited. Tender over both Achilles insertions. Heart: decrescendo diastolic murmur along the left sternal border, unchanged. Lungs clear today. No edema. JVP not elevated sitting.

ECG in office: sinus, normal intervals, nothing new.

A/P:
1. Inflammatory-pattern back pain with heel enthesitis and a brother with AS. Lumbar films including SI joints, HLA-B27, ESR, CRP, CBC today. Continue naproxen as needed meanwhile.
2. Orthopnea in known aortic regurgitation. Starting furosemide 40 mg each morning. BMP today and in 2 weeks. Messaging cardiology so they know and can see him sooner if they want.
3. Flu shot today.
RTC after results.

documents.title: Discharge summary (received 11/1/2024)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 10/22/2024, discharged 10/31/2024. Infectious disease consulting.

Reason for admission: non-healing wound on the bottom of the right foot, with two days of fevers and redness and swelling spreading from it.

Background: type 2 diabetes on insulin, syphilitic aortitis with severe aortic regurgitation followed by cardiology since 2022, ankylosing spondylitis. Remote IV drug use. NKDA.

Findings: 4 cm plantar ulcer of the right foot with purulent drainage and surrounding cellulitis. Foot films without osteomyelitis.
Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus aureus in both sets. Isolate negative for mecA (MSSA), beta-lactamase producing: resistant to penicillin and ampicillin, susceptible to oxacillin, cefazolin, piperacillin-tazobactam, vancomycin and linezolid. Repeat cultures 10/24 no growth.
Given his valve disease, transesophageal echo was done 10/25: no valvular vegetation; known severe aortic regurgitation.

Course: started on vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, changed to cefazolin once susceptibilities returned. Daily wound dressings by the wound care nurse. Fevers resolved by day 3. PICC placed 10/30.

Diagnoses: diabetic foot ulcer, right sole, with cellulitis; MSSA bacteremia.

Discharge medications: cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours through 11/19/2024 (4 weeks from first negative culture) via home infusion; continue metformin, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime, lisinopril 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, naproxen as needed.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; ID clinic in 3 weeks; wound clinic weekly. Weekly CBC and BMP drawn by home infusion, results to ID.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Summary reviewed.

He admits the sore on his foot was there about a month before he went in; thought it was a blister and covered it with a bandaid. No fevers since discharge. Home infusion nurse comes twice a week, he runs the cefazolin himself three times a day, no trouble with the line. Wound clinic saw him Monday.

Exam: vitals reviewed, afebrile. PICC right arm, site clean, no redness. Right sole: wound smaller than the description at admission, clean pink base, no drainage, redness gone. Left foot intact. Heart: murmur unchanged. Lungs clear.

A/P:
- Diabetic foot ulcer with cellulitis and MSSA bacteremia: improving. Finish cefazolin 11/19; ID and wound clinic follow-up as set. Showed him how to check both feet every night with a mirror.
- T2DM: sugars were high in hospital; talked again about control and healing. He wants to keep the same regimen.
- Med rec done, no changes beyond the antibiotic.
RTC January, call sooner for fever or any change in the foot.

documents.title: Home infusion: course complete
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion pharmacy nurse called: last cefazolin dose 11/19, PICC pulled today intact, tip and site fine. Weekly labs during the course were sent to ID, nothing flagged per her. ID visit was 11/18, pt told them he feels well. Foot dressing changes at the wound clinic weekly.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
Non-pressure chronic ulcer of other part of right foot with unspecified severity
Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus infection, unspecified site

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Foot is closed. Wound clinic discharged him before Christmas. ID saw him in November and said the infection is treated, nothing further unless fevers. He checks his feet most nights now.

No fevers, no night sweats. Breathing at baseline, stairs slow.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, afebrile. Right sole: healed, thin pink scar, no callus, no drainage. Left foot intact. Monofilament normal both feet. Heart: diastolic murmur unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
- Right foot ulcer, cellulitis, MSSA bacteremia: resolved.
- T2DM: A1c today. Same meds, again. Footwear talk.
- Severe AR: cardiology echo was due last fall; he has not heard from them. Front desk to call cardiology to get him scheduled.
- Due for dental cleaning, asked if okay: yes, go.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called outside cardiology for overdue echo/follow-up. They have him on a waitlist; first opening is in the spring, they will mail him the date. Pt informed.

documents.title: Eye exam report (optometry)
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 03/11/2025 (overdue from fall). Vision stable. Both anterior chambers quiet, no inflammation. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Follow up one year.

events.reason: fatigue and low-grade fevers after dental cleaning

conditions.label: Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus infection, unspecified site

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 8 hours via PICC through 6/2/2025
Take 4 capsules (2 g) by mouth 30-60 minutes before dental procedures

results.text: Staphylococcus aureus, 3 of 3 sets. mecA not detected (MSSA). Beta-lactamase positive. Penicillin R, ampicillin R; oxacillin S, cefazolin S, piperacillin-tazobactam S, vancomycin S, linezolid S.

reports.text: Mobile echodensities attached to the mitral valve leaflets, consistent with vegetations. Mitral valve prolapse. Aortic root dilated with severe aortic regurgitation, unchanged. Left ventricle dilated, systolic function normal. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Discharge summary (received 6/3/2025)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admission 04/21/2025 to 05/01/2025. Infectious disease service.

Presenting problem: about six weeks of tiredness and on-and-off low fevers. Had a dental cleaning roughly two months before admission and was not given antibiotics beforehand.

Background: severe aortic regurgitation from syphilitic aortitis, mitral valve prolapse, type 2 diabetes on insulin, ankylosing spondylitis, MSSA bacteremia from a foot ulcer in October 2024. NKDA.

On arrival: temperature 37.8 C, HR 90, BP 130/85. A new regurgitant murmur at the apex. Splinter hemorrhages in several nail beds.
Labs: WBC 11.0, hemoglobin 12.5, ESR 45. Blood cultures drawn on admission were pending at first and grew MSSA, same susceptibility pattern as the October 2024 isolate; clearance cultures from 04/24 no growth.
Echo: vegetations on the mitral valve.

Diagnosis: MSSA infective endocarditis of the mitral valve.

Treatment: cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours, six weeks total via PICC (through 06/02/2025).
New: amoxicillin 2 g by mouth before any dental procedure from now on.
Home medications otherwise unchanged.
Follow-up: ID clinic, cardiology, PCP. Weekly CBC, BMP and ESR by home infusion to ID.

documents.title: Home infusion pharmacy
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion pharmacy called to verify PCP for a new referral: pt discharged yesterday on IV cefazolin 2 g q8h through 6/2 for endocarditis. We had no notice of this admission. Requested discharge summary from the hospital. Called pt, he confirms he was in for about 10 days with a heart valve infection. Hospital follow-up booked for 5/7.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
No discharge summary yet (requested 5/2). History from patient and his discharge paperwork.

Admitted 4/21 for weeks of tiredness and low fevers. Told he has an infection on a heart valve (mitral per the paper), the same staph as the foot last fall. Had his teeth cleaned in February and nobody gave him antibiotics first. Home infusion running cefazolin every 8 hours via PICC until 6/2. Has a new prescription for amoxicillin to take before dental visits.

Feels a little better. No fever at home. Breathing at his baseline.

Exam: afebrile, vitals in flowsheet. A few splinter hemorrhages still visible in the fingernails. Heart: diastolic murmur at LSB, plus a soft apical systolic murmur. Lungs clear. PICC left arm clean. No edema.

A/P:
- MSSA mitral valve endocarditis on IV cefazolin: per ID. Med list updated with cefazolin and amoxicillin prophylaxis.
- Severe AR/aortitis: cardiology appointment pending; asked him to keep it.
- T2DM: no change today.
RTC after antibiotics, sooner with any fever.

documents.title: Course complete; summary received
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary from April admission arrived today, scanned and routed to PCP. Home infusion: last cefazolin 6/2, PICC removed this morning. Pt says he feels fine, no fevers.

reports.text: Limited study. Echodensities on the mitral valve leaflets consistent with vegetations. Mitral regurgitation present. Known aortic regurgitation. Left ventricular systolic function normal. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received 6/30/2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 06/23/2025.

CC: fever and tiredness for two weeks.
HPI: 48-year-old man treated for mitral valve endocarditis about two months ago (IV antibiotics finished 06/02). For two weeks he has had fevers and fatigue; a new murmur has been noted. No dental work since. History of IV drug use, remote.
NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.5 C, BP 110/70, HR 105, RR 18.
Exam: painless flat red macules on the palms and soles (Janeway lesions); tender nodules on several fingertips (Osler nodes). Murmur consistent with mitral regurgitation. Lungs clear.
Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250, ESR 45, CRP 20 mg/L. Blood cultures x3 sent.
Bedside/limited echo: mitral valve vegetations.

Impression: suspected infective endocarditis, possible relapse.
Disposition: admitted to medicine with infectious disease consult.

events.reason: ED record received; call to patient

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 8 hours via PICC for 2 weeks (through about 7/7/2025)

documents.title: Follow-up after ED and admission
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 6/23 came in; no inpatient notes. Called him. He was in the hospital until Friday 6/27. Says the blood cultures this time did not grow anything, and ID sent him home with two more weeks of the same IV antibiotic through a new PICC, ending around 7/7. Feels better, no fever since Thursday. Requested the discharge summary. Told him to call the same day for any fever after the antibiotic stops. He wants to skip a visit until the course ends; agreed, nurse will check in.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt: last cefazolin dose 7/7, PICC out yesterday. Says he has felt warm a couple of evenings since Sunday but has not taken his temperature; does not own a thermometer. Advised to buy one, check twice a day, and call the same day for 100.4 or higher. Discharge summary from June still not received; second request faxed.

results.text: Staphylococcus aureus, 2 of 2 sets. mecA not detected (MSSA). Beta-lactamase positive. Penicillin R, ampicillin R; oxacillin S, cefazolin S, vancomycin S, linezolid S.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. PR interval prolonged. QRS duration normal. No acute ST changes. Compared with the 2022 tracing, the PR prolongation is new.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with new first-degree AV block.

reports.text: Limited bedside study. Echodensity on the aortic valve consistent with vegetation. Mild aortic regurgitation on this limited view. Left ventricular systolic function normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Aortic valve vegetation with mild aortic regurgitation.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received 8/5/2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, Sunday 07/20/2025.

CC: fevers, malaise.
HPI: patient with severe aortic regurgitation from syphilitic aortitis, recently treated for infective endocarditis, now two weeks of fever and malaise and a newly noted murmur. Denies chest pain, palpitations and fainting.

Vitals: T 38.5 C, BP 110/70, HR 98, RR 20.
Exam: diastolic murmur loudest at the right second intercostal space. Lungs clear. No focal neurologic deficit.
Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 12.5, platelets 250, ESR 85. Blood cultures sent; preliminary gram-positive cocci in clusters overnight, identified as Staphylococcus aureus.
ECG: first-degree AV block, new.
Bedside echo: aortic valve vegetation, mild aortic regurgitation on limited views.

Impression: recurrent infective endocarditis, now aortic valve, with new conduction delay.
Plan: blood cultures, IV antibiotics, admit to cardiology/ID, formal TEE.

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 8 hours via PICC through 9/1/2025

documents.title: Discharge summary (received 8/5/2025)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, admitted 07/20/2025 from the ED, discharged 08/01/2025. Cardiology and infectious disease co-managing; cardiac surgery consulted.

Summary: third valve infection in 15 months. Blood cultures from the ED grew MSSA (beta-lactamase positive, mecA negative). Clearance cultures 07/23 no growth.
Transesophageal echo 07/22: vegetation on the aortic valve; severe aortic regurgitation (the ED bedside read of mild was on limited views); no perivalvular abscess; mitral leaflets without residual vegetation; dilated aortic root.
ECG: first-degree AV block, stable on daily tracings, no progression.

Diagnoses: MSSA infective endocarditis of the aortic valve, complicated by first-degree AV block; severe aortic regurgitation; syphilitic aortitis.

Plan: cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 hours for six weeks via PICC (through 09/01/2025). Cardiac surgery recommends aortic valve and root surgery once the antibiotic course is complete; clinic visit to be arranged. Continue home medicines. Amoxicillin prophylaxis before dental work continues. Weekly labs to ID.

Note: our records show a June admission at this hospital; summary from that stay is attached in the chart there and will be sent on request.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summaries from 7/20 ED and admission reviewed. June summary never arrived; stopped chasing it.

Third bout of MSSA in a year: now the aortic valve, with a new first-degree heart block. TEE without abscess. On cefazolin to 9/1, then surgery to replace the aortic valve and root is planned. He is scared about the surgery but wants it done. Fevers gone since the second hospital day.

Exam: afebrile, vitals in flowsheet. Tired-looking. Heart: diastolic murmur at both the right upper and left sternal border, bounding pulses. Lungs clear. PICC right arm clean. No edema. No new skin lesions.

A/P:
- MSSA aortic valve endocarditis with first-degree AV block: per ID and cardiology. Problem list updated.
- Severe AR / syphilitic aortitis: surgical consult pending, confirmed the referral is in.
- T2DM: stable, deferred.
- Dental: needs a dental check before valve surgery; reminded about amoxicillin first.
RTC October, or sooner.

documents.title: Home infusion: course complete
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion reports last cefazolin dose 9/1, PICC removed today. Weekly labs went to ID. Pt has cardiac surgery clinic 9/17.

events.reason: surgical evaluation: aortic regurgitation, aortitis, endocarditis

documents.title: Cardiac surgery consultation
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Outside cardiac surgery clinic, 09/17/2025.

49-year-old man with syphilitic aortitis, dilated aortic root and severe aortic regurgitation, treated MSSA aortic valve endocarditis (antibiotics completed 09/01/2025) with first-degree AV block, prior MSSA mitral endocarditis, diabetes, current smoker.

Reviewed TEE from July. Recommendation: aortic root and ascending aorta replacement with a valved conduit. Discussed mechanical versus tissue valve; he prefers to avoid lifelong warfarin and we agree with a bioprosthesis. Dental clearance received. Smoking cessation before surgery strongly advised.

Plan: surgery tentatively early December 2025, pre-operative testing to be scheduled. Call sooner for fever or worsening breathlessness.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw cardiac surgery in September: root and valve replacement with a tissue valve planned for December. He says he is trying to cut down on cigarettes before then.

No fevers since the July stay. Breathing: stairs are harder than they were in the summer, he thinks, but he has been less active. No orthopnea beyond one pillow. No swelling.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. Heart: diastolic murmur, bounding pulses. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact.

A/P:
- T2DM: A1c today. Same regimen. Talked about glucose control for wound healing after surgery.
- Severe AR, pre-op: surgery planned. Precautions given: weight gain, swelling, lying-flat breathlessness, call us.
- Flu shot today. FIT kit from June never came back; he would rather wait until after surgery.
RTC after surgery.

conditions.label: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

reports.text: Portable AP view. The heart is enlarged. Upper lobe pulmonary vessels are prominent (cephalization). Kerley B lines at both lung bases. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Cardiomegaly with pulmonary venous congestion and interstitial edema.

reports.text: The right ventricle is dilated. Large tricuspid regurgitant jet. Left ventricular ejection fraction normal. Aortic regurgitation again seen. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Dilated right ventricle with a large tricuspid regurgitant jet; normal left ventricular ejection fraction.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received 11/4/2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 10/27/2025.

CC: getting more short of breath.
HPI: 49-year-old man with syphilitic aortitis, severe aortic regurgitation awaiting surgery, and recurrent infective endocarditis. Two weeks of increasing breathlessness and fatigue, about 4 kg heavier by his home scale. No chest pain, no fever, no cough. History of IV drug use (remote per prior records).

Vitals: BP 145/55, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air.
Exam: water-hammer pulse. Blowing holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. Pitting edema of both lower legs. Crackles at both lung bases.
Labs: Hgb 13.5, WBC 7.0, platelets 250, creatinine 1.0, BNP 550 pg/mL.
Chest film: cardiomegaly, cephalization, Kerley B lines.
Echo: dilated RV, LVEF normal, large tricuspid regurgitant jet.

Impression: acute heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; tricuspid regurgitation; severe aortic regurgitation.
Plan: IV furosemide, admit to cardiology, notify cardiac surgery.

documents.title: Discharge summary (received 11/4/2025)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 10/27/2025, discharged 11/03/2025.

Admitted with decompensated heart failure (preserved LVEF) in the setting of severe aortic regurgitation and a dilated right ventricle with a large tricuspid regurgitant jet. Diuresed with IV furosemide, down about 4 kg to his usual weight. Edema and crackles cleared, breathing back to his baseline by discharge. Blood cultures negative. Kidney function stable.

Cardiac surgery reviewed: operation moved up to 11/18/2025; tricuspid repair to be added to the aortic root and valve replacement.

Discharge medications: furosemide 40 mg daily resumed, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime, naproxen as needed. Daily weights; call for a gain of more than 1 kg in a day.
Follow-up: pre-op visit at the surgical center; PCP phone check.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after 10/27-11/3 heart failure admission. Feels much better, sleeping flat again with one pillow. Weighing himself every morning, steady since discharge. Taking furosemide every morning. Surgery 11/18; pre-op testing at the surgical center Friday. Reviewed when to call. Reminded him: no smoking before surgery.

events.reason: aortic root and valve replacement; tricuspid repair

reports.text: A. Ascending aorta, resection: aortic wall with chronic aortitis, adventitial and medial chronic inflammation and medial scarring with loss of elastic tissue; findings consistent with the clinical history of syphilitic aortitis. B. Aortic valve leaflets, excision: fibrotic leaflets with changes of healed endocarditis; no active vegetation. Tissue culture: no growth.
reports.conclusion: Chronic aortitis consistent with syphilitic aortitis. Aortic valve with healed endocarditis.

reports.text: Post-operative study. Bioprosthetic aortic valve within a valved conduit, well seated, normal leaflet motion, no paravalvular leak. Tricuspid annuloplasty ring in place with trace tricuspid regurgitation. Normal left ventricular systolic function.
reports.conclusion: Well-seated aortic bioprosthesis without paravalvular leak; trace tricuspid regurgitation; normal LV function.

documents.title: Cardiac surgery discharge summary (received 12/1/2025)
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Cardiac surgical center. Admitted 11/18/2025, discharged 11/26/2025.

Operation 11/18/2025: replacement of the aortic root and ascending aorta with a 25 mm bioprosthetic valved conduit with coronary reimplantation, and tricuspid annuloplasty. Uncomplicated cardiopulmonary bypass.

Pathology: chronic aortitis consistent with syphilitic aortitis; aortic valve with healed endocarditis; cultures no growth.

Course: extubated the same evening. Brief ICU stay. Rhythm sinus with persistent first-degree AV block, no higher-grade block, no pacing required. Chest tubes out day 3. Post-op echo: well-seated bioprosthesis, no paravalvular leak, trace TR, normal LV function.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily (no warfarin), carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 30 units at bedtime. Sternal precautions 6 to 8 weeks. Amoxicillin before dental work for life.
Follow-up: cardiology in 6 to 8 weeks; surgical clinic 2 weeks; cardiac rehabilitation referral placed. PCP within 1 to 2 weeks.

conditions.label: Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus infection, unspecified site

documents.title: Post-operative Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One week out from surgery. Surgical summary not here yet, he brought his discharge folder (summary arrived Monday, reviewed now).

Had the aortic root and valve replaced with a tissue valve and the tricuspid valve repaired on 11/18. Home 11/26. Sore chest, a little better each day. Walking in the apartment and to the corner. Sleeping propped for comfort, not for breathing. Weighing daily, down a few pounds from before the operation. Smoked a few cigarettes since getting home, fewer than before.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Sternal incision clean, edges together, no drainage. Heart regular, crisp valve sounds, soft systolic flow murmur, no diastolic murmur now. Pulses no longer bounding. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.

A/P:
- S/p aortic root/valve replacement (bioprosthetic) and tricuspid annuloplasty: aortic and tricuspid regurgitation fixed; endocarditis treated. Problem list updated. Cardiology in January, surgical clinic next week, cardiac rehab to call.
- First-degree AV block: persists, no symptoms.
- HFpEF: euvolemic, same furosemide.
- Tobacco: strongly advised to stop completely now; offered patch or varenicline, he wants to try on his own.
- T2DM: same meds; labs today with BMP/CBC.
- Dental prophylaxis: amoxicillin, lifelong.
RTC February.

reports.text: Bioprosthetic aortic valve in a root conduit with normal leaflet motion and normal gradients; no paravalvular or transvalvular regurgitation. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated 55 to 60%. Tricuspid annuloplasty ring with trace tricuspid regurgitation. Right ventricle normal in size. Mitral valve prolapse. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normally functioning aortic bioprosthesis. LVEF 55 to 60%. Trace tricuspid regurgitation.

documents.title: Cardiology post-operative follow-up (received 1/27/2026)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, 01/21/2026.

Two months after aortic root replacement with a bioprosthetic valved conduit and tricuspid annuloplasty. Feels well; walking daily, started cardiac rehab this month. No dyspnea at rest, stairs easier than in years. No palpitations or fainting. Still smoking a few cigarettes a day; advised to quit.

Exam: well healed sternotomy. Regular rhythm, soft systolic flow murmur, no diastolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block, unchanged.
Echo: normally functioning bioprosthesis, LVEF 55 to 60%, trace TR.

Plan: continue aspirin 81 mg, carvedilol, lisinopril, furosemide 40 mg. Amoxicillin prophylaxis before dental work. Echo in one year. Return in 6 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Cardiology in January happy with the new valve. Cardiac rehab three times a week, likes it. Still smoking, fewer than before surgery by his account. Back stiff in the mornings as always, naproxen now and then.

Sugars: rehab checks a fingerstick before sessions, and they tell him it runs high.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Sternum healed. Heart regular, soft systolic flow murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact, sensation normal.

A/P:
- T2DM: A1c today. Same metformin and glargine.
- S/p root/valve replacement, HFpEF, first-degree AV block: stable, per cardiology.
- Tobacco: counseled again; not ready to set a quit date.
- AS: stable.
RTC physical in June.

documents.title: rehab
documents.author: patient
documents.body: finished the rehab program today. they gave me a certificate lol. they said keep walking every day which i am doing

documents.title: RE: rehab
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is a real accomplishment, Christopher. Keep up the walking. See you in June.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Turns 50 next month.

Since last physical: a hard year. Third valve infection last summer, heart failure admission in October, aortic root and valve replacement with tricuspid repair in November. Since then steady: walks most days, stairs no problem. No fevers. No red eyes. Mouth sores now and then. Back stiffness in the mornings.
Still smoking, less than before. Alcohol a drink a month or less.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Well. Mouth clear. Eyes quiet. Heart regular, soft systolic flow murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Reduced lumbar flexion, unchanged. Skin intact. Feet: no wounds, monofilament normal.

A/P:
- Preventive: FIT kit given again. Flu in the fall.
- T2DM: labs today; regimen unchanged.
- Valve, HFpEF, AV block: cardiology following; echo due January.
- Tobacco: counseled; offered varenicline again, he will think about it.
RTC September for diabetes.

documents.title: Result note: physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c somewhat lower than winter, still above goal. Kidney and liver tests, CBC, lipids and urine microalbumin as before. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Eye exam report (optometry)
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic exam 07/08/2026. Best corrected acuity 20/20 each eye. No anterior chamber reaction either eye. No diabetic retinopathy. Recheck 12 months.
